evidence.nfc_note: text is unicodedata.normalize('NFC', ...) before sha256 and before storage, so NFD input hashes identically to its NFC form; asserted directly (content_sha256(NFD)==content_sha256(NFC)) and end-to-end (stored meta.text == NFC form, digest == sha256 of NFC bytes). Non-ASCII corpora would otherwise hash differently across runs and refresh would report false change.

next_unit_hint: Verifier (not the author): re-run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_web_fetch.py -q` (expect 52 passed) and independently reproduce both red→green reverts (guard: `if _ssrf_blocked(url, self.allow_private):` -> `if False:`; change detection: replace refresh's old/new comparison with `result.changed = False`). Then confirm `refresh()` on a cached URL still reports changed=false with identical digests, and that `state/webcache` holds <sha256(url)>.json/.txt pairs. Two things a later unit must know: (1) importing resextract.web.fetch executes resextract/web/__init__.py, which U3.1 owns and which imports .search — a broken search.py breaks fetch imports even though fetch.py never imports it; (2) an anomaly worth a second look — the bridge returned only 25 chars for raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/gpt-2/main/README.md while the nanoGPT README returned 12000, so a short crawl payload is accepted as success (only empty/whitespace triggers the scrape fallback); a downstream unit may want a min-length retry or a scrape cross-check for raw-file URLs.
